---
title: "Recommendations for managers"
---

## Near-term actions

- Agree on the management objective and estimand before deployment.
- Maintain a small, manually reviewed reference library for every survey.
- Measure recorder performance and detection range in each representative
  habitat type.
- Keep raw audio, classifier outputs, review decisions, and metadata together.
- Use the same versioned analysis settings across sites and survey periods.

## Study design priorities

Use a staged design: an initial feasibility deployment, a validation study,
and then a powered monitoring study. Include repeated visits or recording
windows so that non-detection can be separated from absence. If response to
restoration is the objective, include reference and treatment conditions and
sample before and after management.

## Governance and reporting

Archive data and code with persistent identifiers, document deviations from
the protocol, and publish assumptions in a form that can be audited. A
managerial decision should be traceable from the question, through the
sampling design and model, to the evidence and its uncertainty.
